kiln_p03_001.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_001.text: The empty credit field belonged to Zhu Yan. Yue recognised the name only after reading the whole packet twice. Seven years earlier, Zhu had helped prepare the shelf whose failed cups now sat beneath the archive stairs. The credit ledger described her as withdrawn before final assessment. Her practice notes described several completed exercises. Neither document told Yue what withdrawal meant. She closed the packet when she heard Zhu approaching. The instinct looked secretive even to herself. Zhu saw the cover's date and knew which shelf she had found.

kiln_p03_002.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_002.text: Zhu set down the tray she had brought and asked whether her old handwriting was still terrible. Yue said she had been looking for the retained body record. That was true but incomplete. Peng came from the next room and told Zhu about the material inquiry, including the possible connection to the old failure. The trimmer studied both women before sitting. She would discuss the firing, she said. Her injury treatment and the reason she had stayed away from the final assessment were different matters. Yue agreed, feeling how easily curiosity could become somebody else's burden.

kiln_p03_003.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_003.text: The old firing had used reclaimed body screened less finely than the maker intended. Zhu remembered the grit because trimming had nicked her blade. She had reported it to the senior worker, who changed the screening task for the next batch. The current archive packet retained that note. It did not establish that grit alone had cracked the entire shelf. There had also been an irregular cooling interval and a partly blocked air passage. Zhu drew the shelf position from memory, marking uncertain corners with a dot instead of making the picture beautifully complete.

kiln_p03_004.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_004.text: The loading-door injury happened the following week, while they were moving ordinary props after a different firing. Zhu had missed the final scheduled assessment because she could not perform its permitted tasks. The workshop recorded withdrawal and closed the trainee line. She received her ordinary wages and treatment support under the old arrangement, but her earlier demonstrated skills never reached the final transcript. For years she had presented herself as a worker who learned on the job. That description was not false. It was smaller than the work she had actually completed.

kiln_p03_005.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_005.text: Peng remembered entering some of those old records. She had been a junior copy keeper, following a template that treated every incomplete final assessment alike. She told Zhu this without asking for immediate forgiveness. Zhu looked at the younger woman she had known beneath the keeper's present title. "I was too tired to read your template," she said. "You were too tired to question it." Peng answered that being tired explained their positions, but the record was still theirs to inspect now. Yue watched a friendship hold an uncomfortable silence without breaking.

kiln_p03_006.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_006.text: Zhu allowed review of the training portion. She did not want a medal, a pity appointment or a story circulated through the yard about what her hand had cost. Peng wrote that scope in the cover. They would distinguish skills demonstrated then from tasks she could perform now. A retrospective record could correct a missing entry; it could not pretend she had completed the later assessment or erase a current physical limit. Zhu agreed, then took up the tray again. The cups on it still needed trimming. Old injustice did not grant them finished feet.

kiln_p03_007.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_007.text: Yue spent the morning searching references, not personal treatment notes. She found three exercise sheets signed by Luo and one inspected batch with Zhu's maker mark on its feet. The marks were already documented before the injury. A fourth sheet carried a blurred signature that might belong to the former senior worker. She set it aside as uncertain. Han teased her for looking as solemn as a judge over a stack of crooked circles. Yue said the circles belonged to somebody. He stopped teasing long enough to bring her a better lamp.

kiln_p03_008.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_008.text: The better lamp revealed a correction on the cooling sheet. Zhu had altered a proposed interval after comparing two retained trial tags, and Luo had signed the explanation. Yue imagined the younger trimmer bent over the same kind of problem Jian now found frightening. It was tempting to make the old worker wiser in retrospect because she had been hurt. Yue resisted that temptation. One of Zhu's other exercises contained a plain numerical mistake. The archive showed a learner improving, not a saint whose every conclusion had been stolen by an ungrateful workshop.

kiln_p03_009.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_009.text: Outside, Jian practised the new schedule exercise with Luo. He had heard that an old record was being reopened, though Peng had not given him Zhu's private account. He asked Yue whether an apprentice could wait seven years for a missing entry. She said waiting that long was not the plan. He wanted a guarantee it would never happen to him. Yue could offer no honest guarantee about every future keeper. She showed him the current signed task scope and the date for its review. He tucked his own copy deeper into the scarf.

kiln_p03_010.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_010.text: Luo reviewed the old sheets after the kiln cooled. His handwriting had become heavier, but the same slash crossed his sevens. He remembered Zhu's trimming assessment because she had argued with him about a foot he wanted narrower. Her wide foot survived the test. His narrow one rocked. He had awarded the demonstrated skill at the time. The transcript's blank was therefore a missing transfer, not a lack of assessment. Peng marked that distinction. Luo stared at the old slate for a moment longer than the evidence required. Some memories were less comfortable when written by one's own hand.

kiln_p03_011.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_011.text: The first corrected entry restored Zhu's assessed trimming and cold arrangement skills. The uncertain cooling sheet remained pending until its signature could be checked against a known example. Nothing was added merely because the total looked disappointingly small. Peng brought the provisional transcript to Zhu privately. Yue stayed outside with Han, who was repairing the lamp handle. She wondered whether the trimmer would feel relieved. Han said relief sometimes arrived late, after annoyance had unpacked its bags. Yue thought he was joking until he explained that he had once waited a year for a broken tool to be repaid.

kiln_p03_012.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_012.text: Zhu emerged carrying the transcript as though it were an ordinary order. She asked Yue whether her own little stand had improved. It had not; she had been copying records instead of trimming. Zhu told her that evidence work was useful, but clay would not learn a shape from her absence. They returned to the cold bench. Yue made another stand, less crooked and too thick. Zhu shaved a thin curve from one side and let her finish the opposite side herself. Old skills had found a line in a book. New skill still needed a patient hand.

kiln_p03_013.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_013.text: The storage-body bars entered their first small firing near the end of the second week. Yue's task was observation from a clear station, with no personal qi connected to the kiln. Ordinary charcoal supplied the heat. A rated supplemental stone assisted the permitted measuring array, and its count belonged to the machine slate. Luo explained the separation while inspecting the cold setup. Yue checked that her ordinary exit route remained open. The distinction felt less like a warning after days among dusty shelves; it felt like knowing which doorway led back to supper.

kiln_p03_014.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_014.text: Jian marked intervals under direct supervision. Han managed the ordinary charcoal feed. Zhu kept the small test vessels' position record, and Yue recorded the independent witness tile readings as taught. A stone in the measuring supply warmed faster than its paired reference. Luo isolated that instrument channel and continued only after the ordinary reference supported the permitted schedule. The faulty stone had not become fuel for Yue. It remained a machine component with an uncertain reading. She wrote the pause and cause beside the interval, leaving enough space for the later cooled result.

kiln_p03_015.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_015.text: The kiln sounded different while working. Cold brick had made the hall seem sturdy and still; heat brought tiny clicks, a low moving roar and the occasional settling thump that Luo could distinguish by place. Yue could not. She asked about two sounds and missed a third because she was looking at her slate. Luo told her to attend to one assigned observation rather than pretend to hear the entire furnace. It was a generous correction. She narrowed her attention, and the next interval became something she could describe rather than endure.

kiln_p03_016.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_016.text: At the meal break, Tan came carrying a purchaser's fresh question about delivery dates. Luo pointed to the closed kiln instead of answering from memory. The test had begun; opening or accelerating it to satisfy an impatient letter would spoil the thing the letter wanted to know. Tan waited beside the cold bench. Jian visibly enjoyed seeing a clerk made to wait. Yue noticed and nudged the boy's empty cup toward the tea pot. He filled it for Tan after a moment's hesitation. The courtesy did not settle their old argument. It made this shift less poisonous.

kiln_p03_017.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_017.text: The ordinary firing finished its heating interval before evening. Cooling took longer than Jian wanted. He stayed near the shutter until Luo reminded him that a watched hot shelf was not a supervised exercise merely because an apprentice refused to leave. The next check belonged to the night worker. Jian handed over the slate, including the instrument pause. He did it carefully enough that the worker asked him to explain the odd mark. That short explanation became another recorded learning task. Yue saw him discover that handing work away could still demonstrate something worth keeping.

kiln_p03_018.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_018.text: They opened the cold kiln the following day within the permitted interval. Most prepared-body bars survived, but the thin test cup showed a small edge defect and one bar cracked through an embedded particle. Luo did not call the whole body useless. It might serve ordinary thick storage ware after appropriate sorting and a revised trial. It had not established suitability for charged teaching cups. Tan had already arranged restoration of the retained fresh stock. The imperfect result made that decision easier to defend and harder to resent. Yue helped carry the cold failed pieces to the archive.

kiln_p03_019.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_019.text: Zhu studied the thin cup's edge. She could trace where ordinary trimming had left a weakness, but the particle near it also belonged to the body. One fault did not cancel the other. Yue had wanted the clay inquiry to produce a single guilty cause. The cup offered two, perhaps more. They labelled the maker process and material observations separately. Han admitted that he had hurried the test vessel's foot because he expected it to be discarded anyway. Luo asked him to remake the cold version properly before using it to judge the material.

kiln_p03_020.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_020.text: The following storage trial would use a sorted portion and a sound test geometry. Its fuel came from the trial reserve counted earlier, leaving no hidden extra firing for teaching ware. Tan obtained a separate revised funding answer before scheduling the fresh teaching sample. Yue watched him make the call and write the conditions correctly. He was capable of careful work. That made his earlier omission more human and more serious. A person did not need to be incompetent at everything to create one harmful gap. She stopped searching his face for an expression that would simplify him.

kiln_p03_021.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_021.text: Peng sent a copy of Zhu's corrected skills transcript to the local apprenticeship registrar, with the uncertain field still identified. Zhu chose to keep the original at home rather than display it over her bench. The registrar's reply would take several ordinary days. The workshop could acknowledge its own assessed exercises now; recognition under the current town standard required another review. Nobody scheduled a public celebration before that distinction was resolved. Yue wondered whether Zhu resented the additional wait. She asked directly while they cleaned the trimming tools. Zhu said resentment and patience were both sitting beside her.

kiln_p03_022.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_022.text: That answer remained with Yue during her settled-work clinic appointment. Two weeks of regular meals and ordinary tasks had improved her usable reserve slightly, without proving a larger throughput. Both established pairs still released within their previous limits. The examiner did not begin a new leg route. She asked what supervision Yue expected for the next stage and what ordinary work would continue during training. Yue had no complete answer yet. The examiner recommended obtaining one before purchasing a practice allowance. A training plan was a real object; longing was only its reason for being requested.

kiln_p03_023.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_023.text: Yue wrote to Su Yan, the examiner who had taught her earlier furnace limits. She described her current job, the recovered checks and the desire to learn the two additional pairs named by the fifth stage. The letter did not assume Su Yan would travel or offer free instruction. It asked whether the kiln town lay within her coming circuit and what a proper plan would require. Yue paid the letter's ordinary carriage herself. She kept a copy beside the wage agreement, where the hopeful question could remain visible without pretending that a teacher's answer had already arrived.

kiln_p03_024.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_024.text: Zhu saw the addressed letter and asked whether Yue had finally written that she wanted to be larger than every accident. Yue said she had written that she wanted training. Zhu approved of the shorter sentence. Then she asked whether Yue planned to remain in the kiln after the nine-week placement. Yue did not know. The larger contract had not been settled, and the local practice plan did not yet exist. Zhu leaned her hip against the bench. "Good," she said. "A question can stay a question without stopping you from making today's cup."

kiln_p03_025.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_025.text: Today's cup improved until Yue lifted it too soon. Its wall bent under the pressure of her eager fingers. She set it down in disgust. Han put the damaged cup beside her earlier stand and declared them an ambitious family. The joke worked only because he then demonstrated how the wall felt when ready. Yue made a second cup and waited. The waiting occupied hands that wanted to fix something. When it finally held its shape, she understood why ordinary patience was not the same as doing nothing. It was an action measured against material rather than mood.

kiln_p03_026.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_026.text: Jian's new schedule exercise progressed to a changed cold arrangement. This time he asked which action the ambiguous hook mark meant before touching a shutter. Luo answered and made the written instruction match. Peng observed the assessment directly. The boy completed the relevant comparisons and explained why a thick jar needed a different cooling assumption from a thin cup. He made one correction after spotting his own error. The recorded skill was not mastery of the live furnace. It was a bounded competence he could carry into the next supervised task without repeating the same uncertainty.

kiln_p03_027.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_027.text: Afterward he asked Yue whether asking the question had counted against him. She asked whether guessing would have produced a better schedule. He rolled his eyes. He had wanted reassurance, not a lesson answer. Yue laughed and admitted that she sometimes wanted praise for refusing to ask questions she needed answered. The boy looked delighted by this confession. He had begun treating her as a powerful visitor, and powerful visitors were less interesting than people who could be teased. They spent the rest of the cleanup inventing impressive titles for their least impressive mistakes.

kiln_p03_028.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_028.text: Peng overheard them call Yue Mistress of the Leaning Foot and Jian Lord of the Wrong Shutter. She said the titles would require a separate register and charged them one clean brush each for consideration. Han contributed the Bent Handle Emperor. Zhu refused a title until they could explain its retirement allowance. For several minutes the archive room filled with ridiculous claims that nobody intended to certify. Yue found the silliness healing in a way no qi wash could be. The same people who argued over real credit could laugh at invented honors without treating every laugh as a threat.

kiln_p03_029.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_029.text: Tan did not join the joke. He passed the doorway with a tightly bound packet. Yue later found him at the outside bench, loosening the string with chilled fingers. His sister had sent a letter . A roof leak had spoiled a sack of their winter grain, and she asked for help with the replacement. He told Yue this before seeming to regret it. She offered no coin. She asked whether he wanted the warmer room to write his answer. He said yes and looked oddly grateful for a help that had no account line.

kiln_p03_030.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_030.text: She left him the room after retrieving her study copy. Through the door she heard him start and stop several sentences. A clerk trained to write other people's terms could still struggle to tell his own family no. Yue remembered the old advance and the credit redirected into its balance. She could understand a temptation to hide a problem until one good order fixed it. Understanding did not permit teaching cups to contain untested body. She wrote that distinction privately, then went to help Zhu move drying boards with an ordinary partner carrying the other end.

kiln_p03_031.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_031.text: Winter deepened around the hall. The outer basin froze at its thin edge, while the centre remained dark and moving. Han broke ice with a wooden paddle and warned Jian not to use a trimmed vessel as a scoop. The boy had already learned that lesson from somebody else's broken bowl. Yue fetched a sound bucket and walked the less slippery path. She could have prepared one permitted reinforced step through an external stitch after an appropriate check, but none was needed. Ordinary good footing solved the ordinary task without creating another practice cost to record.

kiln_p03_032.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_032.text: At the end of the third week, Zhu's registrar reply arrived. The town accepted the documented trimming and cold-arrangement skills under the applicable older programme, while declining to certify the uncompleted final live assessment. The uncertain cooling field needed a better signature reference. Zhu read the decision at her own bench. She touched the line about the accepted work with her left thumb, then resumed trimming the cup she had stopped halfway through. Yue had expected tears. Zhu gave her an amused look. "Were you hoping for a more expensive scene?" she asked.

kiln_p03_033.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_033.text: Later, in the quiet passage, Zhu admitted that she felt younger and angrier than she expected. The record had returned a part of her past, but not the years she had spent describing herself without it. Yue asked whether the workshop should publish the correction. Zhu wanted the institutional error and the improved procedure recorded, with no account of her treatment. She could decide later whether to let her name travel beyond the required register. Peng agreed. Their friendship did not require Zhu to donate every private feeling to the workshop's public learning.

kiln_p03_034.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_034.text: Peng then gave Jian the updated current credit procedure. Each supervised task would identify its teacher, expected skill, ordinary wage portion and review date before it began. An apprentice would retain a copy of the actual completed work. The procedure could still be followed badly. It was useful because a missed step would now be visible before seven years passed. Jian examined the page and asked whether teachers had to sign their own mistakes. Peng said they had to sign the account of what they had taught. The distinction pleased him more than Yue expected.

kiln_p03_035.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_035.text: On her next archive shift, Yue returned to the old failed shelf . The retained body sample survived in a covered jar, and its preparation screen was coarser than the current teaching specification. But the firing slate still contained an unexplained gap during early cooling. Zhu recognised the location of that gap and frowned. She had been present at the bell test before firing. The test had sounded in the yard. The worker needing the live warning had been behind a closed door. Yue placed the two accounts beside each other and stopped believing the clay question was finished.

kiln_p03_036.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_036.text: The current bell hung beside the outer gate, where its cord looked worn from many ordinary hands. Yue stood beneath it and listened while Jian gave one short pull. The note travelled across the open yard and died against the closed drying-room door. Inside, Han heard a dull knock that could have been somebody moving a cart. Luo did not call this proof that every earlier warning had failed. He called it a reason to test the actual occupied posts before another live firing. They wrote the locations down instead of relying on a worker's familiar ear.

kiln_p03_037.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_037.text: Zhu remembered the old worker complaining that the drying room swallowed sound. The complaint had reached her through another apprentice, not through a retained signed note. She made that uncertainty plain. Yue found a maintenance entry for a second hand bell whose location had changed during roof repairs. It might have been intended as a relay. The entry did not name who was responsible for using it. They could repair today's warning path without inventing yesterday's exact sequence. Luo disliked that answer, because an exact sequence would have made the old failure easier to carry.

kiln_p03_038.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_038.text: He showed Yue the scar on the door frame where a hot prop had struck during the old confusion. He had not been hurt. Another worker had burned a forearm and returned after treatment, then left the town the following spring. Luo had written irregular cooling on the failed shelf's card because that was the mechanical result he could see. He had not known how to write a missed warning as a material cause. Yue looked at the old words with less certainty. A card could be accurate and still lead readers away from the question that mattered.

kiln_p03_039.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_039.text: Peng kept the old card and added an inquiry note. The record would retain its original state rather than quietly becoming a wiser document. Then she shut the packet until the shift ended. They had six fresh teaching sample vessels to make under the newly funded plan, and the retained material could not spend all winter waiting for the archive to finish understanding seven years. Zhu asked Yue to help wedge a small clean portion. Yue rolled it too eagerly and trapped a fold. They cut through the fold and began again, where an error could still be handled.

kiln_p03_040.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_040.text: Fresh clay was not a guarantee of a sound cup. Its fine body pulled differently under Zhu's blade, and its water content needed patient adjustment before forming. Yue watched the trimmer leave a slightly thicker foot than the purchaser's drawing suggested. Zhu wanted the sample to test a vessel they could actually make, not a shape that existed only while nobody touched it. Tan copied the real dimensions to the retained plan. He did not argue this time. The supplier's material question had been settled for the sample. The contract's geometry question had not.

kiln_p03_041.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_041.text: Jian made an ordinary trial cup under Han's instruction while the six retained samples stayed separate. His cup looked better than Yue's until he tried to cut the foot free. The wire ran too high and left a slice through its base. He stared at the damage, then asked whether it could be put into the failed-practice rack instead of the reclaim bin. Han agreed after recording what the wire had done. Yue saw the boy want his mistake kept as evidence of work rather than discarded as evidence of unworthiness. It was a surprisingly hopeful request.

kiln_p03_042.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_042.text: Han offered to teach them both the wire movement again. Yue expected him to move faster after so many years. He moved slowly enough that the board seemed to hold its breath. The wire stayed level, his wrists relaxed, and the cup separated without drama. He asked the learners to copy the ordinary posture before touching clay. Jian rolled his eyes at that delay, then found his own elbows too high. Yue recognised the same impatience from her earliest training. Skill often entered through a lesson one's pride had decided was beneath the desired result.

kiln_p03_043.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_043.text: The next day brought wet snow, thick enough to silence the yard and thin enough to turn instantly to slush beneath a cart. The drying-room roof held. Yue noticed because several other roofs did not. A bakery gutter gave way while she was collecting the evening loaves. She helped carry the bread inside, then fetched the owner rather than climbing a ladder into sleet. Zhu arrived a moment later and stood beside the crooked ladder laughing at its ambition. They braced it for the hired repairer, who had ordinary boots and a healthy dislike of dramatic entrances.

kiln_p03_044.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_044.text: The repairer asked Yue to hold the lowest rail while he worked. She kept her feet on clear stone and used ordinary strength. When a wet tile shifted, he stopped and climbed down before moving the ladder. Nothing fell. Nothing exciting happened. Zhu later said this was why good repairs made poor tavern stories. Yue replied that the loaves were a substantial reward. They took them home under the same oiled cloth. At supper, everybody insisted their own slice had been the one personally rescued from the weather. Yue let the claims stand because they harmed no useful record.

kiln_p03_045.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_045.text: Her mother's answer arrived after the snow cleared. The letter contained household news, a complaint about one stubborn kiln door and advice on judging ginger by its cut surface. It did not praise Yue's reserve. Her mother wrote that a bed provided by work should still be checked for damp along the wall, and that being paid on time was not an embarrassment to mention twice. Yue read those lines aloud to her roommates. One immediately inspected the new pipe. The other asked whether Yue's mother took students. Yue laughed until the letter shook in her hands.

kiln_p03_046.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_046.text: She wrote a second reply before the ordinary lamp went out. This time she admitted that clay work made her feel clumsy. Her mother had shaped useful ware for years while Yue had imagined cultivation as a route out of those difficult hours. Now she found herself learning the value of a well-cut foot. The admission hurt a little, as if she had found an old insult hidden inside an ambition she treasured. She did not abandon the ambition. She wanted to carry it without treating the people who stayed at the kiln as people who had failed to travel.

kiln_p03_047.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_047.text: Zhu read that sentiment when Yue asked her help with the phrasing. The trimmer said it sounded honest but too long for someone already busy repairing a door. Yue shortened it to I am learning how much I did not notice. Zhu approved. Then she returned the letter and asked whether Yue would help carry a stool to her neighbor, who had recently come home from an illness. They borrowed a handcart from the house keeper and used the flat lane. The neighbor received the stool with more interest in its height than in the noble intention behind it.

kiln_p03_048.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_048.text: The visit taught Yue something useful about making things for other people. Zhu had measured the neighbor's ordinary seated height before choosing the stool; it let her stand without folding one painful knee too far. A beautiful taller stool would have failed her. The neighbor tested it, asked for a corner to be smoothed and thanked them after the adjustment. Yue thought of the teaching cups, whose thin walls looked graceful in the purchaser's drawing. She asked who would hold them during actual instruction. Zhu said that question belonged in the sample plan before anyone priced another hundred.

kiln_p03_049.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_049.text: Tan could answer only part of it. The association ran beginner classes at three local rooms, each with a different grounding bench. The proposed vessels would hold a modest prepared charge for a short demonstration, but the order did not describe how instructors would interrupt it or replace a damaged cup. Luo requested the actual permitted demonstration method. Tan wrote the request with visible care, then admitted that the association expected the workshop to know what a teaching cup meant. Yue looked at the two differently shaped storage orders on the shelf. Shared nouns had already cost them a week.

kiln_p03_050.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_050.text: The reply would not arrive before the next ordinary jar firing. Luo let the forty storage cups continue under their own tested conditions. Their bodies and dimensions did not require the unanswered teaching method. The six fresh teaching samples remained in slow drying. Yue liked this separation better when it allowed real work to move forward. It was easy to mistake care for a universal stop. Here it meant naming which question affected which shelf. Tan looked relieved when the storage order kept its place. Jian looked disappointed that the entire kiln had not joined his indignation.

kiln_p03_051.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_051.text: Peng noticed Jian's disappointment and asked him to inspect the storage schedule against the cold setup. He found one prop position incorrectly copied and marked it for Luo. The foreman thanked him plainly. The ordinary job was now one mistake safer because the apprentice had looked at it. Jian returned to the archive with less appetite for seeing everything halted. Yue teased him about becoming Lord of the Correct Prop. He said that title lacked grandeur. Peng told him grandeur was available after the sweepings had been removed from beneath the actual prop stack.

kiln_p03_052.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_052.text: The corrected storage shelf passed its cold inspection. Yue watched the ordinary crew arrange a handover for the occupied posts, including the drying room behind its heavy door. A relay bell was tested there with the door closed, and the worker answered the agreed call by appearing at the marked doorway. The trial had no live heat. Its result established that this present warning path could be heard under those conditions. Luo scheduled the corresponding check before the firing, when ordinary noise would differ. Yue understood why yesterday's loud yard note could not certify every room.

kiln_p03_053.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_053.text: Zhu helped mark the relay station, then removed a chair someone had placed across its clear route. The chair belonged to Tan, who waited there for runners. He protested that no one had ever tripped on it. Zhu showed him the path from the closed room to the doorway. He moved the chair into the office, where it blocked his own drawer instead. Yue offered to shift the drawer table. He said he could manage and spent a minute managing loudly. Small changes to a safer arrangement could still feel like theft to the person losing a comfortable corner.

kiln_p03_054.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_054.text: During the storage firing, Jian heard the warning call and passed it to the night worker as trained. Yue observed from her assigned clear station. The relay worked, though the answering worker arrived with flour on her cuff because she had been eating. Luo noted the response interval. No one demanded that workers stop having meals to make the record look perfect. They adjusted the next handover time around the meal break. Yue found this detail unexpectedly moving. The workshop's safety depended on ordinary people remaining ordinary, with appetites and interruptions, rather than becoming ideal figures on a schedule.

kiln_p03_055.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_055.text: The storage cups emerged after their proper cooling interval with a few ordinary rejects and enough sound pieces for the forty-cup order. The workshop had made extras as part of the planned batch, not by conjuring replacement ware afterward. Tan counted the accepted vessels and arranged delivery. Zhu kept the rejected ones for process comparison. The order earned its agreed payment after inspection; it did not certify a teaching charge or settle the old advance automatically. Yue helped wrap the sound cups in clean packing straw. Their plain useful shape pleased her more than the purchaser's grander promise.

kiln_p03_056.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_056.text: One storage cup bore a foot so slightly uneven that Yue almost missed it. Zhu rejected it for the order but asked the bakery whether it wanted a free display vessel marked as such. The owner used it for chalk, where standing perfectly level mattered less. Yue watched the failed commercial cup find an honest ordinary use. It was not sold as a sound water vessel, and its defect was not erased. Jian said the cup had found a better apprenticeship than he had. Zhu replied that it would spend all winter listening to customers argue about bread.

kiln_p03_057.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_057.text: The bakery owner sent back a small loaf in thanks, unasked. Peng entered it as a gift to the shared work table rather than a reduction in anyone's meal provision. Yue was amused by the entry until she remembered how quickly generous extras could become expected wages in another hand. Still, the loaf was warm and they ate it without making a hearing out of kindness. Han declared the chalk cup their most productive employee. Tan, drawn out by the smell, took a slice and finally contributed a ridiculous title of his own: Grand Overseer of Crumbs.

kiln_p03_058.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_058.text: That evening Peng found a known signature matching the uncertain cooling sheet from Zhu's old packet. The former senior worker had signed other retained assessments in the same month. The comparison established who had taught the exercise, while Zhu's corrected explanation and the recorded result established what she had completed. Peng added the field to the retrospective transcript and sent the supported update to the registrar. Zhu looked at the new line and said she remembered hating that exercise. Yue asked whether she hated it less now. "No," Zhu said. "It is mine again, though."

kiln_p03_059.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_059.text: Jian heard only the public procedure update, which said the workshop had corrected an old missing transfer after checking retained evidence. He asked how much paper one person's skill should require. Peng answered that good paper could save a learner from having to reenact every earlier achievement for each new employer. Bad paper could also hide work. Their task was to keep the copy answerable to the actual exercise. Yue added that a cup could answer some questions directly, but it could not say which tired person had made the schedule that kept it intact.

kiln_p03_060.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_060.text: He took that answer into his next ordinary cleanup with more energy than the task deserved. Yue found him stacking frames too high to reach comfortably. He wanted to clear space for the fresh teaching samples before the instructor's method arrived. They lowered the top frames together. He complained that every useful thing seemed to come with another smaller limit. Yue asked whether his arms had grown while he was stacking. He laughed, and the frames settled into a sound lower pile. She wished she could remember the same question whenever ambition made her own reach feel taller.

kiln_p03_061.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_061.text: Su Yan's reply arrived in the fourth week. Her circuit would bring her through the town after another fortnight, with time to review Yue's current plan before considering new instruction. She asked for settled recovered readings, actual paid duties and the proposed practice room's reference specification. Yue read the letter once for hope and again for work. A familiar teacher had not promised a stage. She had named conditions under which the next conversation could become useful. Yue took the letter to Peng, who began fitting the review into the roster without borrowing from Yue's future wage.

kiln_p03_062.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_062.text: Until then, the clinic examiner kept Yue within established-route maintenance. Reserve gradually improved with settled work, but the reading was not forced into a straight upward line. A poor night after the pipe repair still appeared in the history. Yue stopped treating that dip as a stain on her worth. She could compare it with the next recovered check and see an ordinary body responding to ordinary conditions. Zhu said she looked less angry at numbers. Yue answered that numbers had not become more polite. She had begun asking them fewer questions they could not answer.

kiln_p03_063.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_063.text: The association's teaching method finally arrived with a small reference cup in a fitted box. Its walls were thicker than the graceful drawing supplied to Tan. The method used a brief prepared charge through a grounded demonstration lead and required a tested release. Luo placed the actual cup beside the six drying samples. Their feet could fit the bench, but the thin wall design needed review. Tan looked from one to the other and swore softly. The association had wanted the drawing's price while teaching through an object the drawing did not accurately represent.

kiln_p03_064.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_064.text: Zhu inspected the reference cup without admiring its polished glaze. She wanted the rated trial history and the allowed sample variation. The supplied card named a permitted modest load under the association's own bench conditions. It did not cover their kiln body's result, which had yet to be fired. Yue copied the method and the geometry differences into the sample packet. Jian asked whether they should remake all six. Luo said they would test the dried samples as limited material trials, then decide the next design from evidence. The funded shelf would not become a saleable batch by courtesy.

kiln_p03_065.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_065.text: The cold trial plan now had two purposes clearly separated: learn how the fresh body survived its firing schedule, and compare the resulting geometry with the actual demonstration cup. Charging would be considered later on a grounded bench after the ordinary vessel inspection. Yue helped position the samples with enough clear air space to make the first question meaningful. Han watched her hands and said she had stopped trying to make every movement impressive. She was pleased until he added that the result was still occasionally impressive in the wrong direction. Her laugh disturbed none of the cups.

kiln_p03_066.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_066.text: The night before the trial, Tan received another association letter asking for a fixed date for the four hundred vessels. He brought it to Luo instead of answering alone. Luo wrote that no such batch was yet accepted. Their sample firing could fail. Tan asked whether using that word would frighten the purchaser away. Peng said the purchaser was entitled to understand the stage of the work it wanted to buy. Yue expected another argument. Tan only nodded and began the reply. Perhaps a careful answer had become easier because the room no longer required him to invent it privately.

kiln_p03_067.speaker: narrator
kiln_p03_067.text: Yue went upstairs with clay beneath one nail and Su Yan's letter folded beside her study book. Jian's current credits, Zhu's restored old ones and the fresh sample plan all had their own unfinished edges. She no longer wanted to gather them into one uplifting result. The kiln would heat real clay tomorrow, and real clay might crack despite everybody's better intentions. She ate the bread saved by her roommate, washed her hands and slept. Beneath the stairs, the old failed shelf waited without shame. There would be room beside it if the new one failed.
